comparison_frame.description: Fresh matched comparison against the updated upstream library/cache implementation and dependency graph, including removal of the former SonarJS dependency.
comparison_frame.candidate_precision_amendment: Returns nested in for-in/of bodies, including async iteration, now abstain. UUID closure requires every safeParse call to have one direct non-spread argument. These narrowings preserve the fixed corpus; their new adversarial controls belong to the separately qualified native focused suite.

unbiased_sample.population: Fully reconstructable newly added TypeScript-family file occurrences in the archived 550-PR sample, hash-ranked independently of source text with no path/test/generated-content filtering. It does not represent all existing code.
unbiased_sample.interpretation: All forty zeroes remain unlabeled observations, not correctness TN. Compiler/dependency closure was not reconstructed. Test/generated paths were retained by selection; each owner preserves its documented source gates.

labeled_counts.safe_file_count_note: Eight safe files represent seven case files plus one supporting local API module; that support module is not an extra TN case.

performance.method: 3 paired rounds, alternating order; every corpus batch is a fresh native Node process. Cold includes dependency loading and program construction; warm reuses only in-process native parser/program cache. No OS page-cache eviction claim.
performance.scope: Full immutable plugin builds compared with the same two affected owners enabled in both versions. This is not an all-rules application benchmark or a disabled-rule-only control.
performance.interpretation: Shared-VM observations only: candidate cold median was 13.95% higher and wall median 9.98% higher; warm median was 9.33% lower and peak-RSS median 0.40% lower. Paired cold ratios vary from 0.917 to 1.140. These measurements establish neither a speedup nor a general or worst-case overhead bound. Prior qualification timings are preserved separately and are not pooled.
performance.peak_rss_units: KiB on Linux; maximum worker lifetime high-water per paired round, then median of three rounds. Build-process memory is not included.

checker_information_gaps.interpretation: Counts refer to unique source files in one deterministic replicate. Recorded errors include absent project dependencies, synthetic module/JSX/library configuration and deliberate placeholder/invalid fixtures; no failing checker result is reported as a clean application typecheck.

limitations: Two labeled corpus defects remain undetected: a multistatement error helper and a locally aliased UUID schema. These counts apply only to the labeled corpus.
Additional excluded shapes include real returns nested in for-in/of bodies and UUID schemas with any safeParse options/spreads; narrowing proof scope can miss real defects.
The separate malformed fixture is a native parser information gap, not a TN. The forty-file sample itself has no parser failures.

Unresolved dependencies and compiler-profile gaps limit no-hit sample conclusions. Some labeled syntax-flow witnesses also have missing placeholders or declarations; they do not qualify application execution or framework integration.
The local native API model does not prove absence of external monkey-patching; visible local mutation/capabilities withdraw the proof.
Next directive/export syntax and official import boundaries are parsed. Next bundling, registration, services and application imports are not executed.
A raw exception-flow finding does not prove a credential or secret was disclosed.
Three alternating paired fresh-process comparisons provide shared-VM observations, without OS cache eviction, CPU isolation, causal speedup or worst-case cost claims.
Runtime TypeScript 6.0.3 and package metadata 6.0.2 are explicitly distinguished; compiler implementation bytes are not separately attested.

recommendation.promotion: No error promotion or consumer activation is qualified by this corpus.

Normal-build emitted plugin runtime bytes, sources, locked dependencies and standalone corpus configs remain identical. The existing runtime measurements retain their original baseline and timestamps; no new benchmark, build-cache speedup or silent timing repin is claimed.
post_qualification_runtime_reuse.reviewed_project_config_exception: One compilerOptions.incremental=true addition; the tooling config has the same separately verified addition. All other guarded runtime inputs remain unchanged.
post_qualification_runtime_reuse.scope: Original source/API/witness/type-gap/FP/FN and runtime cold/warm/peak-RSS observations remain pinned to their recorded v3 baseline and timestamps. Standalone fixture configs do not extend the changed project configs, and the measured ESM module is byte-identical. No old result or guard was rewritten.
limits: Build/typecheck cache performance and build memory were not measured by v3.
The old corpus measured ESM index.js only. Other JS/CJS identities are preservation observations, not a claim that v3 executed those entrypoints.

Original runtime/compiler-package versions and Zod declaration hashes match. Additional installed entry/compiler hashes are newly recorded observations, not retroactive v3 implementation-byte attestations.
Native canonical checks must still qualify the integrated head; this helper does not replace any required check or native hook.

post_d4d_runtime_reuse.installation_assumption: Normal locked-package and unchanged existing Node installation; no npm install/ci since the historical native TS target. post_d4d_runtime_reuse.qualification_limit: This amendment adds continuity observations only.
